rationale: This is a mechanical splice of two archived variants whose leg decomposition already showed the repurchase and issuance amplifiers to be statistically indistinguishable (fmb 3.606 vs 3.613), so restricting the surprise to the issuance leg is a cosmetic recombination rather than a test of a new economic distinction — and the near-identical stats across every non-negative amplifier tried suggest the whole family is largely a magnitude-weighted rescaling of the same cash-flow-yield value signal.

The archive's two enterprise-anchored variants (gross turnover and net |activity|) already returned the identical fmb of 2.021 and near-identical alphas, strongly implying the enterprise anchor dominates and the amplifier's exact construction is immaterial, so swapping gross turnover for the issuance leg is a low-information variant rather than the coverage breakthrough claimed.

Earnings-to-price is a genuinely untested anchor in this pair's archive and the proposal is honest that it is a discriminating diagnostic (cash-specific mechanism vs. post-1988 sample), though prior evidence that both full-panel equity-based anchors (sales, EBITDA-to-price) were inert makes a null result the likely outcome and the informational value largely negative.

Putting market cap in the denominator of both terms makes the product load mechanically on 1/P², so any apparent improvement will be confounded with a low-price/microcap tilt and the signal ceases to be interpretable as valuation × participation — the exact contamination the proposal concedes but does not design around.

The state-vs-event contrast is a legitimate open question with the now-working cash anchor, and the bounded 0–5 count is the one amplifier that does not merely rescale the value score by transaction magnitude, though it overlaps conceptually with the already-tested within-industry activity indicator (fmb 3.27) and so is more of a robustness probe than a new mechanism.

The stated purpose — determining whether debt raising amplifies cheapness as strongly as equity raising — cannot be answered by an expression that adds sstk and dltis into a single amplifier dominated by the already-tested equity term; a debt-issuance-only amplifier would be the internally consistent test.
